title: Vyberte vizuální svět webu BuildHaven
question: The roll assigned Czech functionalism. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Funkcionalismus
options.lineage: Czech interwar functionalist architecture: white render, ribbon windows, clinker brick, façade lettering
options.thesis: The page is built like the building itself: white render, ribbon-window bands, and the availability shown as the façade's window grid.
options.viewport: Big geometric caps headline on white render. Below it a two-storey window grid (2.NP over 1.NP), each bay one apartment with its area and status, standing on a brick plinth that carries the price and a call button.
options.risk: If the lettering and grid are set timidly, it slides back into a generic white developer site.

raised.raise: Total spot-palette discipline: render white, steel black, and brick red do every job, and gold appears only in the logo mark.
Depth comes only from overlapping flat planes. No drop shadows or gradients anywhere.
One ink for every element: rules, frames, type, and controls are all the same steel black.
Every apartment is a recoverable state: #byt-3 opens that bay, its plan, and its contact, so links can be shared.

options.label: Výkres
options.lineage: the architect's plan sheet: 1:100 linework, pastel unit fills, the razítko title block
options.thesis: The site is the project's own drawing set: the real floor plans lead, and the title block carries the company and contact.
options.viewport: A sheet frame with the floor plan dominant, unit zones in pastel fills, a units table at the side, and the title block bottom-right holding the name and phone.
options.risk: Familiar: architecture and real-estate sites often wear the blueprint look, and it can feel technical rather than homely.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: Availability as a departures board: eight rows, each one a home.
options.viewport: A steel-framed board with BYT, PODLAŽÍ, PLOCHA, and STAV columns; flaps cascade on load.
options.case: Holds product clarity, since the availability board is unmistakable. It loses on audience identification because buyers aren't catching a train, and the cascade risks feeling busy, which you said to avoid.
options.risk: A novelty metaphor that gets old after the first visit.

options.label: Risograph web system
options.thesis: Spot inks misregistered on warm paper.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful zine energy undercuts trust in a large property purchase.
options.risk: Reads as an event flyer, not a home.

options.label: Łowicz papercut
options.thesis: Depth built from layered flat colour.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel built from layers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: folk ornament says nothing about modern apartments.
options.kept: Depth only by overlap, never shading.

options.label: Mondo tech spread
options.viewport: Angled headline slabs over three columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud and busy, which you ruled out.
options.kept: One ink applied to every element.

options.label: Orizuru fold sequence
options.viewport: A centred fold diagram with a numbered step column.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link between folding paper and buying a flat.
options.kept: Every state is deep-linkable and recoverable.

options.label: Riso zine cover
options.viewport: A cover with display type in one ink.
options.case: Fuses poorly: same weakness as the Riso system, and it's a duplicate family.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A typical new-build developer site, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A visualisation hero with the headline and a button, then a row of apartment cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other developer site, the thing you said to avoid.
